subject: Weekly exec highlights — wins, risks & QBR asks
messages:
From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Partner Team <aws-partner-team@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly exec highlights — wins, risks & QBR asks

Morning team — brief weekly readout as we close the quarter. TL;DR: steady momentum on throughput savings, two elevated risks (SLA exception & SOC audit artifacts), and a few ask items to land before the QBR. Attachment: Q2_QBR_prep_deck_v2.pdf (slide deck).

Wins:
- Serving runtime improvements rolled to prod; 12% median token latency reduction on p50 for chat workloads (measured last 48h).
- Dedicated pilot with Acme Analytics passed throughput tests (2.4x expected), preparing partner note.
- Optimize suggestions rolled for three top CPU-heavy routes; estimated $22k monthly savings.

Risks / open items:
1) SLA exception request for a customer migration window (Acme Analytics) — we need leadership sign-off for a limited 48-hour elevated burst above reserved capacity. Request doc attached: SLA_exception_request.docx.
2) SOC evidence gap: Compliance asked for specific log retention hashes for a subset of Private deployments; security is pulling artifacts but timeline is tight (audit window next week).
3) QBR narrative: we lack a short failure-mode example illustrating graceful degradation (for slide 5) — product needs to supply 2-3 screenshots/snippets by EOD Monday.

Asks (owners / deadlines):
- Laura: approve SLA exception template and sign-off route (by Mon 10 AM PT).
- Marissa: consolidate customer success escalation timeline & AEs for Acme (today EOD).
- Karthik: confirm ask to finance on one-time credit for migration test (estimate $8k) so we can present numbers (Mon 12 PM PT).
- Jonas: confirm which deploy variant we want to surface in the QBR demo (pinned stable vs canary).

Notes: I added a short appendix in the deck with raw latency histograms and the partner pilot summary. Happy to talk through in the 1:1s or drop in a 20-min sync if helpful.

-David
David Kim
Head of Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q2_QBR_prep_deck_v2.pdf, SLA_exception_request.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly exec highlights — wins, risks & QBR asks

Thanks David — solid progress and clear asks. Quick responses:

- SLA exception: I support a narrowly scoped exception for the Acme migration test, but want the written rollback/fallback steps in the doc before I sign. Add a one-line risk mitigation (who will throttle, who triggers fallback).
- SOC artifacts: Marissa, can you confirm security has the right contact at Acme to validate retention windows? If not, I will loop in legal to expedite an MSA addendum.
- QBR demo: I prefer we show the pinned stable variant for the live demo and have canary as a backup. Jonas, if the team disagrees, flag now.

Also, please move the SLA request into the shared Drive link you listed and drop a short bullet for the finance ask so I can forward to FP&A.

On the deck: Slide 7 (cost delta table) needs one line clarifying the baseline assumptions used for the $22k saving.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Looping in a condensed CS movement on Acme and the SOC ask:

- Acme migration: AE assigned (Sienna Lopez) confirmed with customer; migration window Feb->Apr was hypothetical in test; we have a 72-hour window they prefer. We requested the 48-hr burst instead to limit exposure. I will push the detailed timeline into the Drive now.
- SOC evidence: security has most artifacts; the missing piece is the retention hash for one on-prem shard. Acme's infra lead is available for a quick call — I will schedule for Monday morning.

Quick OKR check: Engineering OKR #2 (Improve inference cost efficiency) is at 68% completion against our mid-quarter target; we need one more automation to hit 75% before QBR. David — can you prioritize the item labeled "batching-fallback automation" this sprint? That will move the needle.

I'll upload a one-page escalation timeline and the AE contact info to the shared Drive link.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
